reasoning:
I'm checking the renders for positioning issues—the exhaust pipe placement relative to the rear wheel, and whether the barrel element overlaps with the exhaust in the side view.

Let me put the barrel on the right side at x=-0.62, z=-0.45, checking it clears the beacon nearby. I'll keep the jerry can on the same right side too, leaving the left clear for the hero camera angle, and double-check the footpeg positions don't collide with the can's placement.

Next I want to update the hardcoded barrel paint coordinates to match the new position, confirm the fork headstock and front fender look fine from the front view, note the tank decal flame seems a bit small but acceptable, and check the seat's sissy bar backrest texture renders okay before moving on to review the rear fender.

The rear fender, wheel, and shadows look mostly fine, though shadow placement seems slightly off from lighting. The biggest issue is the tail: the rear wheel and exhaust overlap and the exhaust is quite thick, but the chrome tip flare looks okay. Headlight positioning relative to the fork and front wheel checks out in both the 3/4 and front views, as do the cylinder heads flaring at the sides, the flag pennant, and the ape-hanger handlebars — so I'm thinking about improvements like a bigger tank flame decal, chrome rear shocks, and a glowing headlight.

I'm now considering adding a holographic hex emblem sign as a backdrop behind the bike, mounted on posts near the rear of the pad, positioned so it's visible in the three-quarter view without blocking the taillight. I'm calculating where along the pad's hex taper the sign would have enough width to look substantial, checking it against the pennant height and the tail plate/exhaust tip positions to avoid collisions.

I'll use a plane with a hex-cropped alpha texture instead, sized small at the top of the pylon, and extend the rod to support it.

Front fender and brake caliper clipping can be skipped, and the gauge orientation facing the rider looks fine. I'm noting the key edits needed: adjusting barrel positions in three places plus paint and decorative parts, the beacon sign, and the coordinate values for the barrel and jerry can parts.

Adjusting barrel geometry coordinates...

Updating the rod line to include the orange cap detail alongside the beacon changes.
